name: calm dark worn asphalt road with sparse aggregate, long hairline cracks, a repair patch and an oil stain, its unconnected edges crumbling into dirt with a darker broken lip and loose chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road pieces (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, square and large slab)

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain sheet of road autotile pieces on dirt, seen straight down. The silhouette is a full 256-wide rectangle on every row. The column scan shows only repeating texture bands (aggregate, cracks, patch, stain) and no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no roof plane. The road pieces have only a crumbling dark lip on their edges, not a vertical south face. There is no front face of 3 or more rows, so it reads as a flat top-down surface, as expected for ground terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The whole candidate uses only 12 distinct colours, split between dirt and asphalt, so each material has roughly 3-4 lightness steps against Beodeul's 5-6. The asphalt reads as a blue-grey mid tone with speckle and a dark lip, but the 'long hairline cracks', oil stain and patch hardly show. Only the right-hand slab has a faint patch mark with a few dark dashes. The dirt is a noisy 3-tone brown without the clump or grain variety of the references. Measured facts: 5 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 3%, so there are no big flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the crumbling edge is tinted dark blue-grey or brown rather than black, which counts as dark material tone. Structure is fine: crossroads, dead ends and crumbling edges are present. The shading is still shallower and less detailed than the references and does not deliver the described features. When in doubt, fail.
